name: Tamron 16-30mm F/2.8 Di III VXD G2 (Model A064)
notes: Researched as the current successor of the listed 17-28mm F/2.8 Di III RXD (Model A046, 2019): Tamron presents the 16-30mm G2 as the ultra-wide that completes its G2 F2.8 zoom trio, and reviews treat it as the replacement for the 17-28mm. Weight and length are Tamron's Sony E figures; the Nikon Z version is 450 g and 103.9 mm long. Tamron gives maximum magnification as 1:5.4 (wide) to 1:7 (tele); 0.19 is 1:5.4 rounded. Sony E version on sale 31 July 2025, Nikon Z version 22 August 2025, both at USD 929. Internal focusing is stated by The-Digital-Picture's review, not read from a Tamron spec table; zoom mechanism (internal vs. extending) could not be confirmed and is omitted. No optical stabilisation.
famousFor: Tamron's ultra-wide member of its second-generation (G2) f/2.8 zoom trio, adding a wider 16 mm start and the VXD linear focus motor to a compact, light lens with a 67 mm filter thread.
strengths: Sharp in the centre wide open, with sharp corners at f/2.8 from 16 to 24 mm
Fast, quiet VXD autofocus
Light (about 440 g) and takes common 67 mm filters
Very close focusing at 16 mm (0.19 m)
weaknesses: Corners at 30 mm are soft at f/2.8 and need stopping down
No optical stabilisation
Long end stops at 30 mm rather than the usual 35 mm
bestFor: Landscapes and cityscapes with filters on a light kit
Real-estate and interior photography
Street and urban sports at ultra-wide angles
Handheld travel vlogging on a gimbal

name: Tamron 35-150mm F/2-2.8 Di III VXD (Model A058)
notes: Sony E version announced 30 September 2021 and launched 28 October 2021 at USD 1,899; the Nikon Z version was announced in August 2023. Tamron describes it as the first zoom for full-frame mirrorless cameras with an f/2 maximum aperture at the wide end. Tamron gives MOD 0.33 m and 1:5.7 at 35 mm (0.18 = 1:5.7 rounded); the 0.85 m MOD at 150 mm (1:5.9) is from review/database coverage (The-Digital-Picture, Photography Life). Weight and length: Tamron's accessible pages gave them in imperial units (41.1 oz, 6.2 in) for the Sony E version; the metric 1,165 g and 158 mm are from review spec tables and match those figures. Mount-specific Nikon Z weight/length not verified. Filter size left null: one search summary of Tamron's pages said 83 mm while Tamron's accessory listing names an 82 mm front cap, and the conflict could not be settled from a spec table. Minimum aperture not verified (null). Zoom and focus mechanisms not confirmed and omitted. No optical stabilisation.
famousFor: The first full-frame mirrorless zoom to open to f/2 at the wide end, covering 35 to 150 mm with f/2-2.8 so that one lens can replace a bag of fast primes for portraits and events.
strengths: Unusually bright f/2-2.8 aperture over a 4.3x zoom range
Sharp images with attractive background blur for portraits
Fast, precise VXD autofocus
Replaces several fast primes for event work
weaknesses: Heavy and large (about 1,165 g) for a walk-around lens
No optical stabilisation
Expensive by Tamron standards
bestFor: Weddings and events with a single lens

name: Tamron 25-200mm F/2.8-5.6 Di III VXD G2 (Model A075)
notes: Researched as the current successor of the listed 28-200mm F/2.8-5.6 Di III RXD (Model A071, 2020): the G2 widens the short end from 28 to 25 mm and switches to a VXD linear motor. Sony E-mount only. Development announced 9 September 2025, launch announced 21 October 2025, on sale 20 November 2025 at USD 899. Maximum magnification: the launch specification was 1:1.9 at 25 mm (0.16 m MOD); Tamron's lens firmware Ver. 3 (29 July 2026) raises it to 1:2 or greater across 25-70 mm and to 1:1.7 (reported as 0.58x) at 35-50 mm, so 0.58 is the current figure with updated firmware. The 0.8 m MOD at 200 mm is from review/retailer coverage (The-Digital-Picture, B&H), not a directly read Tamron table. Special elements: Tamron mentions XLD and LD glass but the counts could not be verified, so specialElements is null. No VC (Vibration Compensation) in the name or specification, i.e. no optical stabilisation. Zoom and focus mechanisms not confirmed and omitted.
famousFor: Tamron's second-generation full-frame all-in-one zoom for Sony E: an 8x range starting at 25 mm with a bright f/2.8 wide end, near half-macro close focusing and a VXD motor in a 575 g body.

Near half-macro close-ups at the short end

name: Tamron 50-400mm F/4.5-6.3 Di III VC VXD (Model A067)
notes: Sony E version: development announced 27 July 2022, on sale 22 September 2022 at USD 1,299 (price and date from PetaPixel/DPReview coverage of Tamron's announcement). Nikon Z version launched 19 September 2024 at USD 1,299 (Tamron Americas); it weighs 1,180 g and is 185.8 mm long. Weight and length above are Tamron's Sony E figures, without the optional Arca-Swiss-compatible tripod mount, which is sold separately. The 88.5 mm maximum diameter was read from Tamron's Nikon Z listing; the search summary indicated the same diameter for the Sony E version. Built-in VC stabilisation and fast VXD autofocus
1:2 half-macro close focusing at 50 mm
weaknesses: Less sharp at 400 mm than premium 100-400 mm zooms or 400 mm primes
Barrel extends a long way at 400 mm and can wobble slightly

bestFor: Wildlife and birding safaris with a single lens

name: Tamron 150-500mm F/5-6.7 Di III VC VXD (Model A057)
notes: Tamron's first ultra-telephoto zoom reaching 500 mm for full-frame mirrorless. Sony E version on sale June 2021; a Fujifilm X-mount version (Model A057 'X', for APS-C bodies) was announced in September 2022 and a Nikon Z version in October 2023. Figures are Tamron's Sony E values: weight 1,725 g without the included Arca-Swiss-compatible tripod mount (the mount itself weighs 155 g). Tamron gives MOD 0.6 m at 150 mm and 1.8 m at 500 mm, maximum magnification 1:3.1 at 150 mm (0.32 = 1:3.1 rounded). Non-official values: the 7 aperture blades and the launch price come from reviews (ePhotozine, PetaPixel). Launch price is ePhotozine's UK SRP at launch; US figures in the coverage found were inconsistent (PetaPixel about USD 1,400 at launch, another summary USD 1,200), so no USD figure is given. Minimum aperture could not be verified (null). The maximum aperture steps from f/5 (150-237 mm) to f/5.6, f/6.3 and f/6.7 (480-500 mm), per PetaPixel. VC optical stabilisation is built in, but no CIPA stops rating was found. Zoom mechanism not confirmed and omitted.
famousFor: A comparatively compact and affordable 500 mm stabilised zoom that made long-telephoto wildlife shooting accessible on Sony E (and later Nikon Z and Fujifilm X), competing with first-party 200-600 mm lenses on size, weight and price.
strengths: Impressive sharpness for its price class
Smaller, lighter and cheaper than first-party 500-600 mm zooms
Built-in VC stabilisation and fast VXD autofocus
Short 75-degree zoom-ring rotation for quick framing changes
weaknesses: Slow f/6.7 maximum aperture at the long end limits low-light use
Still heavy (about 1.7 kg) for long handheld sessions
Only 7 aperture blades
bestFor: Birds and wildlife at distance
Field sports and motorsport from the sidelines
Airshows
Moon and distant-landscape compression shots
